sequences.header: d2kq5a_ a.298.1.1 (A:) PthA {Xanthomonas axonopodis pv. citri [TaxId: 92829]}

answers.answer:
They share a family because SCOPe classifies the common unit, which is a tandem repeat of about 34 residues. It does not classify total chain length. Each repeat is a helix-turn-helix that packs into the left-handed alpha-alpha superhelix (fold a.298, superfamily a.298.1 TAL effector-like, family a.298.1.1 TAL effector, class a). The three domains differ in how many repeats SCOPe included.

- d2kq5a_ is PthA from Xanthomonas axonopodis pv. citri. It is only a 51-residue SEQRES fragment, annotated 'single repeat'. It covers about one repeat plus the start of the next, with the LTPEQVVAIAS(H/N)(D/G)GGKQALE motif.
- d3v6pa_ is dHax3, a Xanthomonas designer TALE. It is 373 residues, roughly 10–11 near-identical ~34-residue repeats. Repeats differ mainly at the repeat-variable di-residue (RVD, positions 12–13: HD, NG, NI and so on).
- d4cj9a_ is BurrH from Burkholderia rhizoxinica. It is 752 residues, many more repeats, and is a divergent bacterial TALE-like protein.

The length difference therefore comes from repeat copy number. SCOPe flags this directly. d2kq5a_ and d3v6pa_ carry the 're' annotation: 'applies to all domains of a family if the common domain is composed of a different number of small repeating units'. The repeat annotation for the family is anchored on the canonical representative d4cj9a_ (4cj9 A:259-292, one ~34-residue unit). That coordinate range applies to d4cj9a_ itself but not to the other two nodes. The three share the same repeated 34-residue module, so family membership rests on that conserved repeat.

Limits:
- The shared family does not mean the three constructs are equivalent in architecture, repeat count or DNA-binding specificity. Do not transfer RVD specificity, repeat number or function between them.
- Family-level membership here does not make the whole chain length or boundaries comparable. Domain boundaries and repeat counts are crystallographic or construct-dependent. Sequence identity between repeat-rich proteins can reflect internal repeat similarity, not overall alignment.
- d2kq5a_ is a one-repeat fragment, so its family assignment rests on a single repeat unit. It says little about a full superhelix.
- BurrH is more divergent from the Xanthomonas TALEs. Its family placement rests on the repeat structure and fold, which I did not check against any pairwise sequence or structural comparison here.
